Sequential recommenders based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) (Tang and Wang, 2018), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) (Hidasi et al., 2016), and self-attention (Sun et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2019; Kang and McAuley, 2018; Zhou et al., 2020; Rajput et al., 2023) have become prevalent in the era of deep learning. Notably, leveraging a T5-like backbone, Rajput et al. 2023 formalize recommendation as generative retrieval, i.e., autoregressively decode the identifiers of the target items, and achieve the current SOTA. While structurally resembling LLMs, it lacks their pre-training knowledge and the accompanying natural language reasoning potential. Our proposed approach adopts self-attention for sequential recommendation, specifically harnessing LLMs as backbones. We compare against various baselines from all the classes discussed above.

item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports text-informed sequential recommendation, but the retrieved papers do not establish the exact combination of GRU4Rec, corpus-only text learning, and semantic hard negatives. [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) represents items as attribute-text sentences and learns sequential retrieval through pretraining and finetuning; its Transformer backbone is outside this experiment’s family constraint. [JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10512) learns item-text representations through masked representation prediction and reports benefits in low-resource settings, but likewise uses a Transformer and two-stage training. These are architectural inspiration, not direct evidence that a small text encoder trained from scratch will improve GRU4Rec.\n\nA compatible experimental hypothesis: randomly initialized token embeddings, title/description pooling or a small CNN, and a learned projection jointly integrated with item-ID embeddings inside one GRU network. Shared lexical parameters could help sparse items express purpose, artist, franchise, or product relationships; this remains an inference requiring validation. For sampling, [GNNO (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10047) mines hard negatives through item-graph neighborhood overlap, demonstrating an interaction-derived alternative to external semantic models. [R2NS (2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) investigates negative recall and reranking for sequential recommendation. A conservative adaptation would mix random negatives with moderately similar title/description candidates, exclude known training positives, and tune hardness cautiously: similarity can identify plausible positives as well as useful negatives. Compare text integration and sampling separately using the fixed macro validation HR@10; retain one jointly trained GRU checkpoint per category."}
